Watson soon cancelled the rest of his book tour and was suspended from all administrative duties at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory and ultimately removed from his position as chancellor (though the following year he was appointed chancellor emeritus). The ferocity of these attacks upon one of the pre-eminent scientists in the history of genetics and molecular biology is a cautionary tale about the immense social power of Political Correctness. Preposterous assertions are routinely made to deny the variability in average intelligence between the races. A similar assertion is that "race" is an arbitrary classification system and is therefore scientifically invalid. This too is nonsense. All schemes of categorization of natural phenomena are ultimately arbitrary in that they attempt to reduce the essentially infinite list of relevant factors to a manageable subset that allows useful analysis. All of taxonomy is in this sense "arbitrary" but it has proven immensely useful to advance scientific understanding. For example, it is difficult to imagine Darwin developing the theory of evolution had not Linnaeus pioneered the modern system of biological classification. Finally, it is often asserted that the degree of genetic variance between humans is very small, and that the variance between individuals within a racial group is greater than the variance between racial groups. These statements are true but they are irrelevant to the reality of race and the issue of differences between the races in average intelligence. The genetic differences between individuals within a racial group take into account the vast number of traits and characteristics of which intelligence is only one. However, a tiny genetic difference can have a profound effect on a subspecies and it is hardly surprising that when viewing one trait - average intelligence - a very small genetic difference can result in a material variance between human races. The genetic variance between breeds of domestic dogs is less than that between human races. However, no one argues that all dog breeds are the same in average intelligence or that it is immoral to recognize that the average intelligence of border collies is greater than the average intelligence of beagles. Evolutionary forces are constantly at work on all living things, and it is silly to argue that intelligence is not shaped in significant part by genes. Likewise, it is a demonstration of willful ignorance to pretend that average intelligence (as measured by the g factor) does not vary materially between subspecies - including human races. The denial of these facts is the most dangerous challenge facing science in the current age.
